impact_pathways.expected_impact_description: Improved employability and career prospects of MSCA postdoctoral fellows within academia and beyond, through an increased set of research and transferable skills and competences.
impact_pathways.impact_narrative: FIELDWISE improves the fellow's employability and career prospects by consolidating the profile of an Agricultural Data Scientist specialised in plant stress, Earth observation and decision support (OC5). The mechanism is the Career Development Plan (D1.3), agreed by M3 and reviewed at the five steering points M6/M14/M18/M24/M27, coupled with the inter-sectoral AgroVIR placement (WP5, M25-M30) which delivers operational model evaluation, research-to-MVP translation, agricultural-software requirements analysis and exploitation planning. This is a project-specific skills and career progression, not a generic training claim.

impact_pathways.expected_impact_description: Increased and broadened research and innovation impact through enhanced networking and communication capacities with scientific peers and the general public.
impact_pathways.impact_narrative: FIELDWISE broadens its research and innovation impact through the international, inter-sectoral and interdisciplinary collaboration built into the action: the prospective transferability, uncertainty and limited-recalibration report (D3.2, OC3) is produced with the independent commercial-farmer validation setting, and the AgroVIR operational/interoperability assessment (D5.1, OC4) engages a non-academic partner in evaluating the MVP. Communication and networking are carried by the Hungary-Bulgaria bridge (Krumatic in-action; the post-MSCA MVCRI replication route) and the two-way transfer between plant physiology/horticulture and modelling/EO/data science. Concrete FIELDWISE artefacts, not generic networking assertions.

impact_pathways.expected_impact_description: Stronger R&I capacity and output among participating organisations and better transfer of knowledge into research, teaching and education.
impact_pathways.impact_narrative: Tier 3 maps this expected impact (via expected_impact_coverage EI-03) to public-engagement and teaching-integration measures — practitioner-oriented demonstrations of stress/uncertainty outputs, Krumatic-supported farmer-facing demonstrations in Bulgaria, and one public-facing article per year — none of which carry a deliverable id in the Phase 3 WP structure. Per CLAUDE.md §13.3, no deliverable_id may be fabricated to cover this impact. The impact is therefore flagged as uncovered by a named deliverable; Tier 3 explicitly records that Phase 5 may propose a dissemination deliverable while Phase 3 owns the deliverable list.

impact_pathways.expected_impact_description: Increased global attractiveness, visibility and reputation of European participating research organisations.
impact_pathways.impact_narrative: FIELDWISE contributes to the attractiveness and researcher-working-conditions dimension through the Career Development Plan (D1.3, OC5) and the supervision and training arrangements under the re-anchored ATK-hosted governance (Prof. Janda supervision). Charter-consistent working conditions are evidenced at instrument level by the CDP and the documented supervision/training plan; no institutional HR award is claimed for ATK, as its HRS4R status has not been established and must not be assumed. Project-specific mechanism, not a generic reputation claim.

impact_pathways.expected_impact_description: Stimulated innovation and knowledge transfer and expanded career opportunities for researchers by promoting career moves between sectors and organisations through the non-academic placement incentive.
impact_pathways.impact_narrative: FIELDWISE stimulates knowledge transfer and cross-sector career development through concrete transferable research assets: the primary model, benchmark and model card (D2.1, OC2), the crop-transfer specification (D2.2, OC2) and the prospective transferability report (D3.2, OC3). Knowledge transfer is realised by the two-way exchange between the fellow and the ATK/ELTE/MATE environments and by the P1-P2 publications, while the non-academic AgroVIR placement (WP5) supplies the inter-sectoral career move. Each claim traces to a named WP1/WP3 deliverable rather than to generic capacity language.

kpis.description: Career Development Plan agreed and reviewed across all steering points, evidencing the fellow's structured skills and career progression.
kpis.target: Career Development Plan agreed by M3 and reviewed at all five steering points (M6, M14, M18, M24, M27).
kpis.measurement_method: Verification of the signed/agreed CDP document at M3 and of the five recorded steering-point review entries against the CDP.

kpis.description: Prospective transfer gap between research-experiment fit and independent commercial-field performance quantified and reported, not hidden.
kpis.target: Prospective performance, uncertainty and any limited recalibration reported against the predefined criteria; transfer loss stated explicitly.
kpis.measurement_method: Comparison of the frozen primary model's prospective performance against the predefined blocked-validation criteria in the D3.2 report, with uncertainty and recalibration documented.

kpis.description: External non-academic evaluation of the MVP completed by AgroVIR covering operational and interoperability dimensions.
kpis.target: The AgroVIR assessment covers MVP inputs, usability, missing-data behaviour, decision outputs, workflow compatibility and interoperability requirements.
kpis.measurement_method: Confirmation that the D5.1 assessment report addresses each of the specified evaluation dimensions.

kpis.description: Released primary model documented with calibration, uncertainty and blocked unseen-year performance, enabling knowledge transfer.
kpis.target: Primary model and nonlinear benchmark (where justified) reported with calibration, uncertainty and blocked unseen-year performance in one model card.
kpis.measurement_method: Verification that the D2.1 model card documents calibration, uncertainty and blocked unseen-year performance for the primary model and benchmark.

kpis.description: Crop-transfer specification stated, enumerating reusable components and crop-specific validation/recalibration gates for knowledge transfer beyond tomato.
kpis.target: Transferable core components, crop-specific parameters, minimum validation dataset and recalibration gates enumerated for adding a new crop.
kpis.measurement_method: Inspection of the D2.2 specification for the enumerated transferable components, crop-specific parameters, minimum validation dataset and recalibration gates.

dissemination_plan.open_access_policy: All FIELDWISE peer-reviewed publications (P1, P2 and any third paper) are made available in open access in line with Horizon Europe / MSCA open-science requirements. Research data underpinning the released model and validation are managed under a Data Management Plan delivered as a distinct deliverable within the first six months and curated to be Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable (FAIR), with the harmonised 2022-2026 archive, QC flags and metadata (D1.1) documented so that the validation design and model card can be independently scrutinised.

exploitation_plan.ipr_strategy: The exploitation strategy preserves the distinction between the fellow's pre-existing DrR background and the FIELDWISE foreground, so that foreground generated in the action is clearly delimited. The DrR MVP architecture is crop-configurable, with processing tomato supplying the first validated crop module; protection relies principally on software copyright and know-how/trade-secret handling of the models and reusable components rather than on any invented patent claim, with IP handling to support the FMIS-integration and replication exploitation routes. No specific patent is asserted where Tier 3 provides no basis for one.

sustainability_mechanism.description: FIELDWISE results are designed to persist beyond the fellowship through the crop-configurable architecture of the DrR MVP: the validated processing-tomato module and the reusable data-ingestion, uncertainty, visualisation and irrigation-attention components can support later crop modules after crop-specific validation, guided by the crop-transfer specification (D2.2). Continuity is carried by the FMIS integration roadmap (D5.2) built on the AgroVIR external evaluation, which names the interfaces and post-fellowship steps for future integration; by Krumatic's software implementation and Bulgarian farmer-facing uptake; and by the post-MSCA MVCRI replication route that extends reuse toward the wider irrigated high-value horticulture domain. Openly released publications, the model card and the FAIR-managed data ensure the methodological basis remains available for crop-by-crop extension after the project ends.
